definition: Technology entrepreneurship identifies commercial or social opportunities and builds ventures around technically enabled products or services.
example: A founding team tests whether clinics need its scheduling prototype before committing to a product launch.

definition: Theatrical techniques are methods performers and production teams use to convey a story, direct attention or shape an audience's experience on stage.
example: A director uses a freeze in movement to draw attention to a key line.

definition: Thyroid cancer is a malignant growth originating in thyroid tissue.
example: A cancer registry classifies a tumor arising from thyroid follicular cells as a thyroid cancer.

definition: Thyroid diseases and disorders affect the thyroid gland's structure or its production of hormones that regulate metabolism.
example: A clinician investigates whether a patient's symptoms reflect inadequate thyroid hormone production.

definition: TL 9000 is a quality management framework for the information and communications technology industry that adds sector-specific requirements and performance measurements to ISO 9001.
example: A telecommunications equipment supplier tracks defect and reliability indicators as part of its TL 9000 quality program.

definition: In linear algebra, the trace of a square matrix is the sum of its main diagonal entries.
example: The trace of a diagonal matrix with entries two and five is seven.

definition: A traumatic brain injury is a disruption of brain function or structural injury to the brain caused by an external force.
example: A clinician evaluates a person for a brain injury after a fall followed by confusion.

definition: Twisted pair is a cable construction in which two insulated conductors are wound around each other to reduce electromagnetic interference.
example: An Ethernet installation uses twisted pairs to transmit signals between devices.

definition: Urban resilience is the capacity of a city and its communities to anticipate, withstand, adapt to and recover from disruptions.
example: A coastal city designs alternate routes and emergency services to remain functional during floods.

definition: Urban sustainability concerns meeting a city's social and economic needs while limiting long-term environmental harm and resource depletion.
example: A city pairs transit investment with affordable housing near stations to reduce dependence on private cars.

definition: Urological disorders affect the urinary tract or the male reproductive organs.
example: A urology service evaluates a patient with recurring kidney stones.

definition: Use of force concerns the application of physical compulsion and the legal, ethical and organizational standards that govern it.
example: An oversight team assesses whether the force documented in an incident complied with policy.
sense_note: The relevant standards depend on the setting and jurisdiction.

definition: Utility engineering concerns the design, construction and operation of infrastructure that provides services such as power, water, gas or communications.
example: Engineers coordinate water and electrical routes before a street reconstruction.

definition: Utility frequency is the nominal rate at which alternating current cycles in an electrical power grid.
example: A motor specification identifies whether it is intended for a 50-hertz or 60-hertz supply.

definition: VA loans are mortgages that eligible borrowers can obtain with backing from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
example: A lender checks whether a prospective homeowner qualifies under the VA home loan program.

definition: Virtual health provides healthcare services or support remotely through digital communication and monitoring technologies.
example: A patient meets a clinician by video for a follow-up appointment.

definition: A virtual LAN logically segments devices into separate data-link networks even when they share physical switching equipment.
example: An office places guest devices and employee computers in different VLANs on the same switch infrastructure.

definition: A virtual private network extends private connectivity over a shared network using logical tunnels, commonly protected by encryption.
example: A worker uses a VPN to access internal company resources from a remote location.

definition: Virtual reality presents an immersive computer-generated environment that can respond to a user's viewpoint or actions.
example: A trainee uses a headset to practice navigating a simulated facility.

definition: Visual impairment education adapts instruction and materials for learners who are blind or have low vision.
example: A teacher provides tactile diagrams and accessible text for a geometry lesson.

definition: Wage and hour laws govern matters such as minimum wages, compensable time, overtime and recordkeeping.
example: A payroll team checks whether a work schedule generates overtime under the applicable rules.

definition: Warehouse automation uses machines and software to perform or coordinate warehouse tasks with less manual intervention.
example: An automated storage system retrieves a tote and delivers it to a packing station.

definition: Wave phase specifies a position in a repeating wave cycle relative to a reference, typically as an angle.
example: Two signals with the same frequency are in phase when corresponding peaks occur together.

definition: A waveguide confines and directs the propagation of waves along a path.
example: A microwave waveguide carries electromagnetic energy between a transmitter and an antenna.

definition: Welding symbols are standardized drawing annotations that specify weld locations, types, dimensions and related requirements.
example: A fabricator reads a drawing symbol to identify which side of a joint requires a fillet weld.

definition: Wi-Fi architecture describes how wireless local-area networks organize stations, access points and connections to other networks.
example: A campus plans several access points to let devices connect across its buildings.

definition: Wi-Fi security uses controls such as authentication and encryption to protect wireless networks and their communications.
example: An organization gives staff and guests separate authenticated access to its wireless service.

definition: A wide area network connects devices or local networks across geographically separated locations.
example: A company links offices in different cities through its wide area network.

definition: The Windows Vista startup process is the sequence through which firmware and boot components locate and load Windows before it starts system services and presents sign-in.
example: A technician distinguishes a boot-manager error from a failure that occurs after Windows begins loading.

definition: Wine education develops knowledge and judgment about wine production, regions, styles, tasting and service.
example: A class compares how two fermentation choices affect a wine's flavor and texture.

definition: Wireless technologies transmit information without a physical cable between communicating endpoints, most commonly by radio waves.
example: A sensor sends measurements to a nearby gateway by a low-power radio link.

definition: Women's studies examines women's lives and experiences and the ways gender shapes social, political and cultural institutions.
example: A researcher studies how women's labor was documented during a period of industrialization.

definition: Word formation examines processes that create new words or lexemes, such as compounding, derivation and blending.
example: A linguist explains how snow and ball combine to form snowball.

definition: Workforce trends are changes over time in the size, composition, skills or work arrangements of a workforce.
example: A planner compares the age distribution of employees over several years to estimate retirement exposure.

definition: Worship ministry is organized religious service supporting the planning and conduct of communal worship.
example: A worship coordinator prepares music and readings for a congregation's service.

definition: Yahoo! Messenger protocols were communication formats and rules used by the Yahoo! Messenger service to exchange messages and status information.
example: A computing historian examines how clients represented whether a contact was available.
sense_note: Historical implementations differed by client and protocol version.

definition: Youth ministry is organized religious work that supports young people's spiritual development and participation in a faith community.
example: A youth leader organizes age-appropriate discussions and volunteer activities.
